Subject: Telemetry & misuse monitoring questions (RFP)

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. Our security and platform teams had a few follow-ups specifically around telemetry and misuse monitoring. I've attached a short spreadsheet with numbered questions to keep answers mapped to the RFP. Topline items we care about:

- Sampling and aggregation: can you provide expected sample rates for prefix caching, KV cache hits, and anomalous-rate sampling?
- Alerts & SLAs: what are detection-to-notification timelines for high-severity misuse signals?
- Evidence exports: formats and retention for logs we can ingest into our SIEM (JSON/NDJSON preferred).
- PII handling: redaction options and whether token-level logs can be suppressed per-tenant.
- Triage workflows: do you provide automated triage metadata (confidence scores, matched policy IDs)?

Could you either attach answers inline (numbered) or share a short doc? We may ask for a short technical walkthrough the week of May 24.

Appreciate it — Emma

Subject: Re: Telemetry & misuse monitoring questions (RFP)

Hi Emma — thanks for the spreadsheet, received and reviewed. Below are concise answers aligned to your numbered questions (full export attached as PDF and CSV for your engineers). If useful we can expand any item in the walkthrough.

1) Sampling & aggregation: Default telemetry sampling is event-level 100% for alertable signals and 5-20% for routine generation traces depending on model type and token rate. We offer a configurable sampling policy per-tenant and per-route (options: 0%, 1%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 100%). Prefix/KV cache hit metrics are aggregated at 1m and 1h buckets; anomalous-rate sampling can be set to stream full-traces when thresholds are crossed.

2) Alerts & SLAs: For high-severity misuse signals (policy-defined blocklist hits, critical abuse patterns) we have an internal detection-to-notify objective of 15 minutes; customer-configurable push notifications (webhook/Slack) average delivery <30s after system detection. Incident acknowledgement SLA for Dedicated/Enterprise plans: 1 hour; full triage timeline depends on incident scope.

3) Evidence exports: Logs can be exported in NDJSON, Parquet, or CSV. We provide a pre-built SIEM ingestion template for Splunk/SumoLogic/Datadog. Retention is configurable per-tenant (default 90 days); longer retention available as an add-on. Exports include anonymized tokens by default; token index mapping can be provided under NDA for forensics.

4) PII handling: We support on-ingest redaction and token suppression toggles. Customers may opt to disable token-level logging for sensitive routes; streaming aggregates (counts, flags) remain. We also support customer-managed KMS for keying PII during transit and at rest.

5) Triage metadata: Every detection includes a policy_id, confidence score (0-1), matched pattern snippet, and sampling context (route, model, sequence length). We include a suggested severity mapping and remediation notes in the exported evidence bundle.

I've attached a two-page summary (redwood_telemetry_summary.pdf) and a csv of our canonical metric definitions (misuse_metrics_definitions.csv). Propose a 45m technical walkthrough on May 25 (11:00-11:45 PT) — does that work?

Diego / Rachel — forwarding proposed clarifications for the walkthrough and the RFP response. Key edits: clarify "anomalous-rate sampling" as a dynamic policy (not fixed by model) and emphasize the availability of hashed token maps only under NDA. Also confirm recommended default thresholds we should propose to Safeguard:

- Anomalous-rate trigger: +3 sigma over baseline requests per minute (configurable)
- High-severity detection confidence threshold: >= 0.85
- False positive review window: 48 hours for automated score adjustments

I attached a short snippet for the SIEM template that shows field names and example NDJSON rows. Recommend we commit to the 45m walkthrough and surface the Dedicated SLAs as an option if they need faster incident response.

Marissa Cole

Hi Emma — quick summary and commitments following our internal review. See inline and attached for the full export.

- Sampling: configurable per-tenant with presets (1/5/10/20/100%). We will propose 5% default for production generative routes, 100% for policy-triggered traces. Dynamic anomalous sampling will stream full traces when the +3 sigma trigger crosses baseline.
- Alerts & notification: detection-to-notify objective 15 minutes for high-severity; push delivery options via webhook/Slack/email. For customers on Dedicated plans, we can commit to a 1-hour incident acknowledgement SLA and prioritized remediation support.
- Evidence & exports: NDJSON/Parquet/CSV exports, Splunk and Datadog ingestion templates attached. Default retention 90 days; can be extended under contract.
- PII & redaction: on-ingest redaction and per-route token suppression available. Hashed token maps for deterministic mapping available under NDA and KMS controls.
- Triage metadata: policy_id, confidence (0-1), matched snippet, model version, route, and sampling context included in every detection bundle.

Next steps: confirm the May 25 11:00 PT walkthrough or propose an alternate time. We will include the Dedicated SLA language and an export sample in the meeting deck.

Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough.
